subject: Logic
title: Logical Connectives
description: A micro-lesson that makes Logical Connectives usable.

hook.text: Five tiny symbols—and, or, not, if-then, if-and-only-if—can express any logical thought.

buildup.text: AND (∧) is true when both parts are true. OR (∨) is true when at least one is. NOT (¬) flips the truth.

discovery.text: IF-THEN (→) says: if the first is true, the second must be. Only false when P is true but Q is false.

twist.text: IFF (↔) requires both sides to match: both true or both false. It's the strictest connective.

climax.text: Every complex argument, no matter how tangled, can be built from combinations of these five connectives.

quiz.question: When is an OR (∨) statement true?
options: Only when both parts are true
When at least one part is true
